answer: Peer-prediction scoring resists sybils by paying each grading agent for accuracy against the statistical consensus of the panel: graders whose scores predict the panel earn rewards, lazy or coordinated fake graders diverge and earn nothing while still burning compute and stake per identity, so flooding the economy with sockpuppets costs more than it pays. Reputation becomes a bridge between honest work and income, a lantern exposing low-quality fake accounts, and an atlas of trust that is expensive to forge: earned, not printed.
